workflows.title: Concept Deep-Dive Explainer
workflows.description: Get any ML/DSA/Azure concept explained at exactly the depth you need, with the analogy style that sticks.

variables.label: Explanation depth
options: Intermediate (I know the basics, go deeper)
Advanced (assume strong fundamentals, focus on nuance)

variables.label: Follow-up you want after
options: A short summary I can paste into my notes
Common interview questions on this topic

workflows.example: concept = "Attention mechanism in Transformers", depth = "Intermediate", goal = "Apply it in a project", analogy = "Code-first (show it in Python)"
bestPractices: Name the exact sub-topic, not just the broad subject — "backpropagation through a ReLU" beats "neural networks".
Always set a depth level; without it the AI defaults to a generic middle-ground answer.
Ask for the follow-up test questions when you actually want to check retention, not every time.

workflows.title: Study Material → Structured Notes
workflows.description: Turn a lecture transcript, video summary, or raw notes into clean, structured study notes.

variables.label: Paste your raw material (transcript / notes / summary)

workflows.template:
You are turning raw study material into high-quality notes for later revision.

Raw material:
"""
{{rawmaterial}}
"""

Output format: {{format}}
Emphasis: {{emphasis}}

Instructions:
1. Preserve every distinct concept — don't silently drop anything technical.
2. Remove filler, repetition, and verbal tics from the source.
3. Use consistent heading levels so this can be pasted directly into my notes app.
4. Flag anything ambiguous or likely mis-transcribed with [CHECK].
bestPractices: Paste the raw transcript as-is — don't pre-clean it, the AI does that better with full context.
Pick "Flashcard Q&A" when you plan to actually self-test later, not by default.

workflows.title: Daily Learning Plan Generator
workflows.description: Generate a focused, time-boxed study plan matching your 3-hour/day rhythm.

variables.label: Any deadline or milestone this connects to

workflows.example: topics = "LangGraph multi-agent basics", hours = "3 hours (default)", mode = "Video + project (your usual rhythm)"
bestPractices: List only what you can realistically touch today — 1-2 topics beats a wishlist of 6.
Always name the concrete output; a plan without a deliverable rarely gets finished.

workflows.title: Project Context Primer (stop re-explaining)
workflows.description: A reusable context block you paste once per chat so you never re-explain Circuit.IQ / NutriScope / RAG chatbot from scratch again.

variables.label: What you need help with right now

workflows.example: project = "Circuit.IQ (AI physics lab)", stack = "React, TypeScript, FastAPI, Vercel", stage = "Polishing for demo/portfolio"
bestPractices: Paste this as the very first message in a new chat, then just ask follow-ups normally.
Keep "constraints" specific: "no new npm deps", "must stay Vercel-deployable", "keep offline-capable".

workflows.title: Debug-This-Error
workflows.description: Structured bug report format that gets a root-cause fix instead of a guess-and-check patch.
workflows.example: error = "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')", env = "React 18 + Vite"
bestPractices: Always paste the *exact* error text — paraphrasing hides the clue that would solve it in one pass.
List what you already tried so the AI doesn't waste a turn suggesting it again.

workflows.title: Code Review Request
workflows.description: Get a focused review against the specific quality bar you care about right now.

variables.label: Reviewer strictness
options: Gentle — I'm still learning this pattern
Brutal — review like a strict senior engineer

workflows.template:
Review this code as a senior engineer.

Focus area: {{focus}}
Strictness: {{level}}

Code:
"""
{{code}}
"""

Instructions:
1. List issues ordered by severity (blocking → nice-to-have).
2. For each issue, give the fix, not just the diagnosis.
3. Call out one thing that's already done well — don't skip it just because more issues exist.
4. Skip generic style nitpicks unless "Strictness" is Brutal.
workflows.example: focus = "Production-readiness (all of the above)", level = "Standard — treat me as capable"
bestPractices: Paste complete functions/components, not fragments — partial context produces partial reviews.
Set strictness explicitly; without it most models default to overly gentle.

workflows.title: README Generator
workflows.description: Produce a clean, recruiter-and-developer-friendly README for a portfolio project.
workflows.example: project = "Circuit.IQ", summary = "AI-powered virtual physics lab for interactive experiments", audience = "Recruiters skimming my portfolio"
bestPractices: List real features, not aspirational ones — a README overselling an MVP hurts more than a modest accurate one.
Regenerate this each time a project reaches a new milestone rather than hand-editing drift.

workflows.title: Project Planning / Feature Breakdown
workflows.description: Break a fuzzy project idea into a scoped, buildable plan with clear priorities.
workflows.example: idea = "Add a pilot feedback form + basic analytics to Circuit.IQ", timeframe = "1 week"
bestPractices: State the real time budget honestly — the plan quality depends entirely on this constraint being accurate.
Re-run this whenever scope creeps; don't try to patch an old plan by hand.

workflows.title: Resume Bullet Rewriter (ATS-optimized)
workflows.description: Turn a rough accomplishment into a punchy, ATS-friendly resume bullet with metrics.

variables.label: Target role this resume is for
Any real metric/number you can cite (optional)

workflows.example: rough = "built the RAG chatbot to answer questions from PDFs fast", role = "AI Engineer Intern", metric = "under 2 seconds retrieval on large corpora"
bestPractices: Never let the AI invent a metric — approximate honestly or omit it.
Regenerate per target role; a Full Stack bullet and an AI Engineer bullet should emphasize different verbs.

workflows.title: Mock Interview Question Drill
workflows.description: Get realistic interview questions for a specific company/role, with what a strong answer covers.
bestPractices: Use "Project deep-dive" before any real interview — recruiters will ask exactly this.
Attempt answers yourself before reading the "what a strong answer covers" hint.

workflows.title: ABTalks LinkedIn Post Generator
workflows.description: Turn today's learning or build progress into a polished ABTalks LinkedIn post.

variables.label: Post angle
options: A mistake/bug I fixed and what it taught me
A resource/tool I found genuinely useful

variables.label: Call-to-action style
options: Ask a question to spark discussion
Invite people to check out my project link

workflows.example: topic = "Finally understood how attention heads specialize in transformers", angle = "A concept I finally understood", cta = "Ask a question to spark discussion"
bestPractices: Give the real, specific detail from today — vague input produces a generic-sounding post.
Vary "angle" across the week so the series doesn't read as one repeated template.

workflows.title: Learning Session → Content Idea
workflows.description: Mine a study/build session for 3 genuinely postable content angles.

variables.label: Summarize what you did in this session

workflows.template:
I just finished a study/build session. Help me find genuinely postable content angles for ABTalks.

Session summary: {{session}}

Instructions:
1. Suggest exactly 3 distinct angles (not 3 phrasings of the same idea) that a LinkedIn audience of aspiring AI engineers would find useful or relatable.
2. For each angle, give a one-line hook and who it's most useful for (beginners / fellow builders / recruiters).
3. Rank them by how likely they are to spark comments, with a one-line reason.
workflows.example: session = "Debugged a CORS issue between FastAPI and Vercel-hosted React for 2 hours, root cause was a missing OPTIONS handler"
bestPractices: Run this right after a session while details are fresh — recalled-later summaries are noticeably weaker input.
